questions.stemHtml: The disaccharide shown below is present abundantly in which of the following food?
questions.solutionHtml:
Milk
  • As the bond is β(1→4) bond, we can easily identify this molecule as lactose. Because only lactose has beta-bond. Other common disaccharides usually have α-bonds (see other figures)
  • Lactose is the major sugar in milk.




Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No.84

questions.stemHtml: The type of transport mechanism across the membrane shown in the picture is known as:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ping pong

This is the Ping Pong mechanism of transport shown.

  • In the PING state, the carrier is loaded. Then conformational change occurs.
  • In the PONG state, the carrier is unloaded towards the other side of the membrane.
  • This occurs in the case of facilitative transport for glucose i.e. GLUTs.




Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 477

questions.stemHtml: A section of intestinal brush border membrane is shown in the picture. Identify the glucose transporters present at marked points X and Y:
questions.solutionHtml:
X-SGLT-1, Y-GLUT-2
  • In the intestine, both facilitative transport (GLUT) and secondary active (SGLT) transport are present.
  • At the apical membrane, on the Luminal side of intestinal cells, SGLT-1 (Sodium dependent Glucose Transporter-1) is present. It transports glucose and galactose in a Na+ coupled symport.
  • At the basolateral membrane towards the interstitial fluid side, facilitative transporter GLUT-2 is present that transport glucose from the intestinal cell into blood using facilitated diffusion.
  • In kidneys also (see fig below), both facilitative transport (GLUT) and secondary active (SGLT) transport are present.




Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 481

questions.stemHtml: The type of isomerism between two isomers of glucose shown in the image below is known as:
questions.solutionHtml:
Enantiomerism
  • Isomerism in which there is different H & OH orientations around the Penultimate/Reference/2nd last carbon
  • Isomers are also known as mirror images of each other e.g. D-and L-Glyceraldehyde and D-glucose and L-glucose.
  • If at penultimate carbon -OH is on right it is given the designation as D isomer and if -OH is on left it is given the designation as L isomer (See fig below).

Note: As seen in glucose, the orientation of -H and -OH changes at all of the chiral carbons but for giving D- and L- notations, we look at the penultimate carbon/2nd last carbon. That’s why it is also known as reference carbon.

  • The sugars abundantly present in human is D-form whereas L-amino acid are abundantly present in the proteins.



Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry 7th Edition page no. 242

options.label: D
options.text: D-Enantiomer of glucose at C-2 and C-3

questions.solutionHtml:
Epimer of glucose at C-2

This structure shown is Mannose.

  • Epimerism is different H and OH orientation at one chiral center.
  • Mannose is an epimer of glucose at C-2.




Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 149

Optical isomerism
  • In the picture, it can be observed that a plane-polarized light is passed through the solution. After passing through the solution, the light gets rotated. This phenomenon is Optical isomerism.
  • If the light is rotated towards the right side, then the sugar present in the solution is known as dextrorotatory (d) or (+).
  • If the light is rotated towards the left side, then the sugar present in the solution is known as levorotatory (l) or (-).
  • These dextro and levo are optical isomers.




Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 149

questions.stemHtml: Identify the kind of channel. This channel is associated with which of the following transporter:
questions.solutionHtml:
SGLT-1
  • The sodium potassium ATPase pump is shown in the picture. It is associated with SGLT i.e. sodium-dependent glucose transport.
  • SGLT transport is also known as secondary active transport as the energy is not directly used for sugar transport but rather is used indirectly when sodium ions are pumped out of the cell using a Na+-K+ pump and in the process consuming ATP.




Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 481

questions.stemHtml: The bottle shown in the figure contains:
questions.solutionHtml:
D (+) glucose

Option A: D (+) glucose

  • This is a bottle used for IV injection of Dextrose
  • An abundant form of carbohydrate in our body is always the D form
  • 'D’ means structural isomer i.e. Enantiomer with OH on the right side at C5 carbon in glucose
  • (+) or (d) means dextrorotatory. Glucose is always dextrorotatory (d) (+).
  • The solution of glucose is known as Dextrose. Therefore, Dextrose is D (+) glucose



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 149

questions.stemHtml: Powder Puff or Hedge Hog appearing osazones in the given figure belong to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Lactose

Option B: Lactose

Osazones

  • All reducing sugars will form osazones with an excess of phenylhydrazine when kept at boiling temperature.
  • Osazones are insoluble and each sugar will have a characteristic crystal form of osazones.
  • Powder Puff or hedgehog-appearing osazones are from lactose.



Vasudevan Textbook of Biochemistry for medical students 6th edition page no. 64

questions.stemHtml: Given is the structure of glycogen. What is the linkage at points ‘a’, ‘b’, and ‘c’ respectively:
questions.solutionHtml:
α1→4, α1→6 and α1→4

Option C: α1→4, α1→6 and α1→4

  • In the structure of glycogen,
    • linear chains have α (1→4) bonds.
    • Only the branching point has α(1→6) bond
  • Point ‘a’ and ‘c’ lies in a linear Point ‘b’ lies at the branch point.




Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 153
